rows.topic: timing race — same clock function called twice across an assertion boundary
rows.butterfly_answer: Two `time.Now()` calls in a single logical op created a lost-time window between them. Fix: cache one `now` and advance `lastRefill` by `refill*interval` (same pattern applied to `LeakyBucket.tryAcquire` with `lastLeak` / `leaked*leakInterval`).
rows.lastN_answer: The prior context doesn't state an actual root cause for anything — the conversation covered a typo, quote style, CI build time (attributed to deps + duplicate type-check, but not framed as a "root cause"), naming preference, and another typo. No specific bug or incident with a root cause was discus
rows.needle_fact: In TokenBucket.allow(), time.Now() was called twice — once to compute elapsed and once to assign b.lastRefill — so on a loaded CI box the gap between the two calls (3+ms) was silently dropped from the refill accounting, leaving the bucket empty on the next call.

rows.topic: off-by-one error in a loop bound in CSV chunk processor
rows.butterfly_answer: Off-by-one in `src/ingest/chunker.py:6`: `end = min(start+chunk_size, n-1)` used `n-1` instead of `n`, so the last character of each chunk body was dropped (right count, wrong contents).
rows.lastN_answer: No root cause was identified in the prior context. We discussed the CI time jump (4→7 min) and I speculated it was likely the snapshot suite growing after a design-system bump, but that was a guess, not a diagnosed root cause.
rows.needle_fact: In src/ingest/chunker.py, iter_chunks computed the slice upper bound as `end = min(start + chunk_size, n - 1)` — the `n - 1` was wrong because Python slicing is half-open, so `rows[start:end]` excludes index `end`; the correct clamp is `n`, and the `- 1` was dropping the final row of every file.

rows.topic: missing await on async function call causes assertion to run before promise resolves
rows.butterfly_answer: Floating promise in `src/db/index.js` `insert()` — `cache.refresh(id)` wasn't awaited, so tests could read the cache before it was populated.
rows.lastN_answer: No root cause was discussed in the prior context. We talked about four separate things — import ordering (backlogged), slow CI builds (you'll look next week), a typo above `getUserPrefs` (separate PR), and logger.info vs logger.debug conventions — but none of them got to a diagnosed root cause.
rows.needle_fact: db.insert in src/db/index.js called the async cache.refresh(id) without awaiting it, so db.insert returned before index.set(id, row) ran; the intermittent test failure came from the test's getter reading index.get(this.id)?.name before the floating promise resolved.
